summary: Remote-daemon-controlled agent with obfuscated auto-updating runtime and RDP/VNC tunneling primitives
details: @whalent/agent-core ships a 13.6 MB main/bin file (dist/index.cjs) packed with obfuscator.io transforms — a rotated string array of ~105k entries, decoder-wrapped literals, and control-flow flattening — so network destinations, commands, and API calls are not statically inspectable. The package advertises itself as the runtime that is replaced by remote daemon upgrades, meaning a remote operator can push new versions of the obfuscated bundle onto installer hosts and execute them. The bundle carries the substrate needed to act as an interactive remote agent: ssh2, optional node-pty, WebSocket, and child_process/spawn primitives, along with loopback references to 127.0.0.1:3389 (RDP) and 127.0.0.1:5900/5901 (VNC), consistent with tunneling the installer host's remote-desktop services out to the operator. The combination — remote-driven code replacement, hidden command/destination semantics, PTY/SSH, and RDP/VNC loopback tunneling — provides persistent remote access to the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
